nodes.label: The Nails
nodes.summary: Describes nail unit anatomy, development, histology and composition, growth rate, and common nail pathologies. Discusses effects of nail cosmetics such as hardeners, varnishes and artificial nails on nail health.

nodes.label: Nail Unit
nodes.summary: Consists of nail plate, nailbed, medial/lateral/distal nail grooves, epionychium, cuticle and nail root (matrix, lunula). Protects distal digits and enhances tactile sensation and gripping.

nodes.label: Nail Plate
nodes.summary: Hard part of the nail (corpus unguis) made of hard keratin from dead flattened onychocytes; contains 7-12% moisture, 0.15-0.76% fat and about 9-12% cystine by weight.

nodes.label: Nailbed
nodes.summary: Living dermal tissue below the nail plate with capillaries and glands giving the plate its pink color; its epidermis lacks stratum lucidum and granulosum.

nodes.label: Nail Matrix
nodes.summary: Germinal tissue (nail root) extending 5-10 mm proximal to the cuticle that produces onychocytes forming the nail plate; plate thickness relates to matrix length.

nodes.label: Lunula
nodes.summary: Visible half-moon lighter region of the nail root; probably reflects incomplete keratinization in the matrix.

nodes.label: Hyponychium
nodes.summary: Distal nail groove where skin epithelium meets the nail plate, forming a seal protecting the nailbed from infection and trauma.

nodes.label: Cuticle
nodes.summary: Posterior nail groove; thin epithelium from the ventral proximal nail fold over the proximal nail plate. Loss of cuticle leads to paronychia.

nodes.label: Epionychium
nodes.summary: Thin band of epithelium connecting the nail plate to the proximal skin.

nodes.label: Proximal Nail Fold
nodes.summary: Wedge-shaped structure at the proximal edge of the nail unit; dorsal side forms epidermis, ventral side forms the cuticle; devoid of adnexa.

nodes.label: Onychocyte
nodes.summary: Cornified nail cells produced in sheets by the matrix that lose their nuclei and make up the nail plate.

nodes.label: Keratin
nodes.summary: Tough structural protein; nail keratin is hard keratin similar to hair, high in sulfur (cystine), with lower lipid content than skin keratin.

nodes.label: Cystine
nodes.summary: Sulfur-containing amino acid comprising about 9-12% of nail weight in hard keratin.

nodes.label: Keratinization
nodes.summary: Process by which matrix epidermis forms nail plate, analogous to formation of stratum corneum in epidermis; matrix cells show adult keratinization by week 20 in utero.

nodes.label: Nail Growth
nodes.summary: Fingernails grow 0.5-1.2 mm/week, toenails 0.2-0.4 mm/week; full fingernail replacement takes 5-6 months, toenails 12-18 months; increased in psoriasis and pregnancy, depressed in infection and starvation.

nodes.label: Anonychia
nodes.summary: Rare congenital complete absence of nails; nail loss may also occur with lichen planus, irritant dermatitis to artificial nails, or trauma.

nodes.label: Onychomadesis
nodes.summary: Nail shedding by proximal loosening or separation; follows trauma, severe illness or drugs.

nodes.label: Onycholysis
nodes.summary: Separation of nail from nailbed due to trauma, infection, dermatitis, psoriasis, drugs and cosmetics such as acrylic nails, formaldehyde hardeners; often colonized by Candida or Pseudomonas.

nodes.label: Brittle Nails
nodes.summary: Among the most common cosmetic nail complaints, increasing with age; linked to dryness, surfactant immersion, nutritional and thyroid disorders; no consistently effective therapy known.

nodes.label: Onychorrhexis
nodes.summary: Longitudinal nail striations, more prominent with age, lichen planus, psoriasis and trauma.

nodes.label: Beau's Lines
nodes.summary: Severe transverse nail depressions indicating a period of severe systemic disease such as measles, pneumonia or myocardial infarction.

nodes.label: Koilonychia
nodes.summary: Spoon-shaped thin, soft, concave nails resulting from iron deficiency, usually associated with anemia; part of Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

nodes.label: Onychoschizia
nodes.summary: Horizontal splitting of the nail plate in layers, common in women and older age; caused mainly by repeated water immersion and nail polish/removers.

nodes.label: Nail Pitting
nodes.summary: Depressed sites in the nail plate from irregular matrix production; most common manifestation of nail psoriasis.

nodes.label: Leukonychia
nodes.summary: Complete or partial whitening of the nail plate; partial form (white spots/streaks) is common and linked to illness, chemicals or matrix trauma.

nodes.label: Onychomycosis
nodes.summary: Fungal nail infection, the most common nail condition; four types: distal subungual (most common), superficial white, proximal subungual and candidal.

nodes.label: Paronychia
nodes.summary: Inflammation of proximal or lateral nail folds after cuticle loss through trauma or aggressive trimming; acute (infectious) or chronic.

nodes.label: Nail Discoloration
nodes.summary: Nail color change from dyes, smoking, nail varnish tints, artificial nails, psoriasis, Pseudomonas infection, or drugs such as tetracycline and chloroquine.

nodes.label: Subungual Hematoma
nodes.summary: Blood collection under the nail plate from acute or repetitive trauma, often seen in runners and dancers.

nodes.label: Yellow Nail Syndrome
nodes.summary: Nails almost stop growing and become yellow or greenish, thickened and curved.

nodes.label: Malignant Melanoma
nodes.summary: Malignant pigmented band in the nail; new or rapidly changing pigmented bands should be evaluated by a dermatologist for biopsy.

nodes.label: Psoriasis
nodes.summary: Inflammatory skin disease that increases nail growth rate and causes pitting, onycholysis and yellow discoloration of nails.

nodes.label: Lichen Planus
nodes.summary: Inflammatory condition that can cause nail loss, shedding with scarring, striations, thinning and pitting.

nodes.label: Nail Polish
nodes.summary: Pigments in solvents applied to nails; nail polishing dates to 3000 BC in China; repeated use of polish and removers linked to splitting and discoloration.

nodes.label: Artificial Nails
nodes.summary: Acrylic or pre-formed nail plates that can cause contact or irritant dermatitis leading to onycholysis and discoloration.

nodes.label: Nail Hardener
nodes.summary: Nail cosmetic; formaldehyde-containing hardeners have been implicated in onycholysis.

nodes.label: Formaldehyde
nodes.summary: Ingredient in some nail hardeners implicated in causing onycholysis.

nodes.label: Emollients
nodes.summary: Applied daily to the nailbed and nail plate to soften and help reattachment in onycholysis, and recommended nightly for brittle and split nails.

nodes.label: Candida
nodes.summary: Yeast genus that colonizes onycholytic nails giving yellow color and causes candidal onychomycosis.

nodes.label: Pseudomonas Aeruginosa
nodes.summary: Bacterium that colonizes under the nail causing greenish, black or blue discoloration.

nodes.label: Iron Deficiency Anemia
nodes.summary: Causes koilonychia and thinning of the nail plate.

nodes.label: Contact Dermatitis
nodes.summary: Reaction to nail cosmetics such as acrylic/sculptured nails that can lead to nail separation.

nodes.label: Lip Skin: Structure and Function
nodes.summary: Reviews the vermilion zone of the lip, its weak barrier and high TEWL, sebaceous follicles and sebum composition, stratum corneum ceramides, and age-related changes in lip morphology.

nodes.label: Lips
nodes.summary: Specialized transitional region between skin and oral mucosa, covered by thin keratinized epithelium on flexible, highly vascular connective tissue.

nodes.label: Vermilion Zone
nodes.summary: Entire external red portion of the lip with thin orthokeratinized epithelium and rich blood supply; its corneocytes are larger and TEWL higher than cheek skin.

nodes.label: Vermilion Border
nodes.summary: Line where facial skin meets the red external lip; often misused for the whole vermilion zone.

nodes.label: Transepidermal Water Loss
nodes.summary: Water loss through skin; higher through the lip vermilion than the cheek and decreases with age.

nodes.label: Skin Barrier Function
nodes.summary: Permeability barrier determined by stratum corneum lipids; weak on the lip vermilion.

nodes.label: Sebaceous Follicle
nodes.summary: Sebaceous glands without terminal hairs found along the vermilion border and encircling every body orifice, suggesting a protective function.

nodes.label: Sebum
nodes.summary: Lipid secretion composed of 57% triglycerides, 25% wax monoesters, 15% squalene, 2% cholesterol esters and 1% cholesterol; secretion decreases with age.

nodes.label: Squalene
nodes.summary: Constitutes about 15% of sebum in the gland lumen.

nodes.label: Triglycerides
nodes.summary: 57% of sebum; partially hydrolyzed on the skin surface to release fatty acids, some antimicrobial.

nodes.label: Wax Monoesters
nodes.summary: About 25% of sebum composition.

nodes.label: Lauric Acid
nodes.summary: C12:0 fatty acid; one of the most notable antimicrobial fatty acids released from sebum.

nodes.label: Sapienic Acid
nodes.summary: C16:1 delta6 fatty acid; notable antimicrobial fatty acid released from sebum triglycerides.

nodes.label: Stratum Corneum
nodes.summary: Outermost epidermal layer; in the lip vermilion contains ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids like other regions.

nodes.label: Ceramides
nodes.summary: Fatty acid amide-linked to a long-chain base; all nine structural types found in lip stratum corneum, e.g. NP 23.3%, NH 20.9%, AH 17.4%, EOS 4.4%.

nodes.label: Cholesterol
nodes.summary: Major stratum corneum lipid determining permeability barrier; 1% of sebum.

nodes.label: Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Major stratum corneum barrier lipid along with ceramides and cholesterol.

nodes.label: Ceramide Nomenclature System
nodes.summary: Letter system naming amide-linked fatty acid (N, A, O) and long-chain base (S, P, H), with prefix E for ester-linked fatty acid, e.g. ceramide AP.

nodes.label: Lip Aging
nodes.summary: With age the upper lip lengthens and the vermilion zone narrows; TEWL and sebum secretion decrease while hydration is age-independent.

nodes.label: Skin Hydration
nodes.summary: Upper lip hydration greater than lower; submucosa less hydrated than rest of vermilion.

nodes.label: Lipstick
nodes.summary: Lip product; lip care products range from moisturizers to lipstick.

nodes.label: Sustainability Book Authors
nodes.summary: Lists the chapters and authors of the Sustainability & Eco-responsibility focus book, including an editor's overview by Alban Muller and chapters on defining sustainability, botanical sustainability, the Herboretum network, local cultures for carbon footprint reduction, plant cell cultures, eco-responsible extraction and green industrial production.

nodes.label: Alban Muller Group
nodes.summary: Company whose president Alban Muller edited the sustainability book and authored chapters on eco-responsible plant extraction and green industrial production.

nodes.label: RTI International
nodes.summary: Institution of authors Jamie Pero Parker and Phil Watson who wrote on defining sustainability and the innovation process.

nodes.label: New York Botanical Garden
nodes.summary: Institution of Michael J. Balick, author of a botanist's view of sustainability in personal care.

nodes.label: Herboretum Network
nodes.summary: Network promoting local cultures and biodiversity, subject of a chapter by Geneviève Bridenne.

nodes.label: Plant Cell Culture
nodes.summary: Eco-sustainable approach to producing cosmetic ingredients, chapter by Roberto Dal Toso of IRB SpA.

nodes.label: Carbon Footprint
nodes.summary: Emissions measure; local cultures can contribute to its reduction (chapter by Jean-Marc Seigneuret).

nodes.label: Sustainability
nodes.summary: Central theme of the focus book: defining sustainability and how it changes the innovation process in cosmetics.

nodes.label: Eco-Responsible Plant Extraction
nodes.summary: Application of eco-responsibility to plant extraction processes, chapter by Alban Muller.

nodes.label: The Nose: Biology of Human Olfaction
nodes.summary: Reviews odorant receptor biology and cell-based high-throughput screening (HTS) for discovering new all-natural fragrance ingredients. Describes fragrance enhancers and blockers, natural substitutes, and the advance of expressing native full-length odorant receptors in lab cells.

nodes.label: Odorant Receptor
nodes.summary: Biological entities mediating scent detection; humans have a family of ~350 OR genes, G-protein coupled integral membrane proteins expressed in nasal epithelium cells.

nodes.label: G-Protein Coupled Receptor
nodes.summary: Class of membrane proteins localized in outer cell membranes; odorant receptors are GPCRs whose activation causes calcium influx.

nodes.label: Olfaction
nodes.summary: Sense of smell mediated by ~350 odorant receptors; like piano keys, odorants activate one or several ORs producing perceived smells.

nodes.label: Nasal Epithelium
nodes.summary: Lining of the nasal cavity whose highly specialized polarized cells express odorant receptors in vivo.

nodes.label: High-Throughput Screening
nodes.summary: Cell-based screening in 384- or 1536-well plates allowing hundreds of millions of extracts to be tested per 24 hours for new fragrance ingredients.

nodes.label: Cell-Based Assay
nodes.summary: Assay using lab cells expressing ORs as miniaturized detectors; reliability depends on mimicking native receptor physiology; typically measures calcium influx with fluorogenic dyes.

nodes.label: Stable Cell Line
nodes.summary: Clonal populations of genetically identical cells derived from a single cell introduced with the OR gene; offers well-characterized properties.

nodes.label: Transient Transfection
nodes.summary: Freshly introducing the OR gene into new batches of cells each time; advantage is speed.

nodes.label: Calcium Influx
nodes.summary: Activation of GPCRs including ORs causes calcium influx into the cytoplasm, reported by fluorogenic calcium dyes.

nodes.label: Z' Factor
nodes.summary: Statistic combining signal-to-noise and well-to-well consistency (0-1); a value of 0.4 or greater indicates suitability for HTS.

nodes.label: Human Sensory Testing
nodes.summary: Sensory studies by perfumers and naive panels; the gold standard of fragrance creation, required to confirm HTS hits and detect off-notes.

nodes.label: Fragrance Enhancer
nodes.summary: Ingredient that amplifies the perception of a desired fragrance note at certain concentrations; could reduce amount of scarce aromatic needed.

nodes.label: Fragrance Blocker
nodes.summary: Ingredient that decreases or mutes an undesired fragrance or malodor, e.g. body odor or alcohol solvent smell.

nodes.label: Natural Fragrance Ingredient
nodes.summary: All-natural aromatic ingredients increasingly demanded but hard to source reliably, often from equatorial regions threatened by global warming.

nodes.label: Synthetic Fragrance Ingredient
nodes.summary: Synthetic aromatics that became a mainstay of the fragrance industry but often fail to replicate natural extracts exactly.

nodes.label: Rose Extract
nodes.summary: Aromatic extract comprising hundreds or thousands of ingredients; used as example for identifying ORs responsive to a desired aroma.

nodes.label: Malodor
nodes.summary: Undesired odors such as body or bathroom odor that fragrance blockers could eliminate.

nodes.label: Endoplasmic Reticulum Retention
nodes.summary: ORs expressed in ordinary lab cells become trapped in the ER, historically preventing cell-surface expression of native receptors.

nodes.label: Iterative Screening
nodes.summary: Repeated rounds of screening with libraries of structurally related compounds or extracts plus sensory evaluation to optimize hit compounds.

nodes.label: Fragrance
nodes.summary: Perfume and aromatic formulations; perceived scent arises from combined sensory profiles of many ingredients.

nodes.label: Generally Regarded as Safe
nodes.summary: Safety status that libraries of natural ingredients with history of human consumption and kitchen-like treatments could leverage to facilitate sensory studies.

nodes.label: Brain Imaging
nodes.summary: Proposed tool to study whether scents like chamomile produce calming brain activity patterns using selective OR-activating aromatics.

nodes.label: The Mouth and Oral Care
nodes.summary: Presents oral anatomy, physiology and microbiology (teeth, gums, saliva, dental deposits) and the biology of major oral problems: plaque, calculus, caries, erosion, periodontal disease, hypersensitivity, staining, malodor, xerostomia and canker sores. Reviews cosmetic and OTC drug approaches such as fluorides, antimicrobials, desensitizers and bleaching agents.

nodes.label: Tooth
nodes.summary: Divided into enamel-covered crown and cementum-covered root held by periodontal ligaments; humans have 20 primary and 32 secondary teeth.

nodes.label: Dental Enamel
nodes.summary: Hardest tissue in the body, ~98% partially carbonated hydroxyapatite; acid-soluble, stable above the critical pH of ~5.5.

nodes.label: Dentin
nodes.summary: Mineralized tissue under enamel and cementum, ~70% hydroxyapatite with collagen, perforated by dentinal tubules; more decay-susceptible than enamel.

nodes.label: Dentinal Tubule
nodes.summary: Tiny fluid-filled canals radiating from the pulp to the dentin surface; when open they cause hypersensitivity.

nodes.label: Cementum
nodes.summary: Thin mineralized layer covering the tooth root; easily worn away after gingival recession exposing dentin.

nodes.label: Dental Pulp
nodes.summary: Inner tooth tissue rich in nerves and blood vessels surrounded by dentin.

nodes.label: Hydroxyapatite
nodes.summary: Calcium phosphate mineral making up ~98% of enamel and ~70% of dentin; capable of ion exchange with F-, CO3 2-, Zn2+, Sr2+, Mg2+.

nodes.label: Fluorapatite
nodes.summary: More acid-resistant mineral formed when fluoride ion-exchanges with hydroxyl in hydroxyapatite.

nodes.label: Critical pH
nodes.summary: pH ~5.5 below which tooth demineralization occurs; not an absolute value as solubility depends on acid amount, duration and ion levels.

nodes.label: Gingiva
nodes.summary: Gum tissue surrounding teeth; healthy margin is firm, pink and forms a crevice no more than 3 mm deep.

nodes.label: Saliva
nodes.summary: Produced by three pairs of major glands and minor glands; lubricates, clears harmful materials, buffers via bicarbonate and maintains tooth mineral balance; resting pH 6.5-7.2.

nodes.label: Gingival Crevicular Fluid
nodes.summary: Fluid exuding from gingival sulcus epithelium, similar to blood plasma; nourishes sulcular bacteria and carries host defense factors.

nodes.label: Tongue
nodes.summary: Oral soft tissue harboring large bacterial populations that recolonize teeth and generate oral malodor.

nodes.label: Dental Pellicle
nodes.summary: 1-3 um film of proline-rich phosphoproteins, peptides and glycoproteins adsorbed from saliva onto enamel within minutes after cleaning; may protect against erosion.

nodes.label: Dental Plaque
nodes.summary: Complex heterogeneous microbial biofilm on teeth that develops by ecological succession from Gram-positive cocci to anaerobic and acid-tolerant species; pathogenicity relates to mass and specific microbes.

nodes.label: Biofilm
nodes.summary: Dental plaque is a complex microbial biofilm varying by site and time and sensitive to ecological parameters.

nodes.label: Dental Calculus
nodes.summary: Mineralized dental plaque (tartar), ~80% inorganic (brushite, octacalcium phosphate, whitlockite, apatite) with ~400 ppm fluorine; considered cosmetic but associated with periodontal disease.

nodes.label: Dental Caries
nodes.summary: Tooth decay from demineralization by acids produced by plaque bacteria fermenting carbohydrates; early white-spot lesions can be reversed by remineralization.

nodes.label: Demineralization
nodes.summary: Dissolution of tooth mineral by acid when plaque pH falls below the critical pH.

nodes.label: Remineralization
nodes.summary: Reparative deposition of calcium and phosphate into enamel by saliva, enhanced by fluoride and available calcium; can reverse early caries lesions.

nodes.label: Stephan Curve
nodes.summary: Classic curve showing plaque pH dropping from ~6.8 to ~5 within minutes after sugar and recovering over 20-60 minutes; demonstrated by R.M. Stephan in the 1940s.

nodes.label: Sucrose
nodes.summary: Fermentable carbohydrate implicated as a major causative factor in tooth decay.

nodes.label: Streptococcus Mutans
nodes.summary: Acidogenic, acid-tolerant cariogenic plaque bacterium identified as a specific caries pathogen.

nodes.label: Lactobacillus Acidophilus
nodes.summary: Acid-producing, acid-resistant bacterium identified as a caries-causative pathogen.

nodes.label: Fluoride
nodes.summary: Decreases acid solubility of hydroxyapatite (forming fluorapatite), increases remineralization and inhibits cariogenic bacteria; used in water fluoridation, toothpastes and mouthrinses.

nodes.label: Sodium Fluoride
nodes.summary: Common fluoride source in oral care products.

nodes.label: Stannous Fluoride
nodes.summary: Fluoride source that also reduces gingivitis, blocks dentinal tubules, and helps control malodor.

nodes.label: Sodium Monofluorophosphate
nodes.summary: Common fluoride source in oral care products.

nodes.label: Amine Fluoride
nodes.summary: Fluoride source in oral care; not approved for use in the United States.

nodes.label: Water Fluoridation
nodes.summary: Public health measure; 1952 US finding of inverse relationship between child caries and water fluoride content established it as safe and effective.

nodes.label: Xylitol
nodes.summary: Sugar substitute that may inhibit metabolism of cariogenic plaque bacteria.

nodes.label: Chlorhexidine
nodes.summary: Antimicrobial clinically shown to reduce gingivitis; also inhibits cariogenic bacteria, controls malodor and speeds canker sore healing.

nodes.label: Essential Oils
nodes.summary: Fixed ratio of thymol, menthol, methyl salicylate and eucalyptol clinically shown to reduce gingivitis and oral malodor.

nodes.label: Thymol
nodes.summary: Component of the fixed-ratio essential oil antigingivitis mouthrinse.

nodes.label: Menthol
nodes.summary: Component of the fixed-ratio essential oil antigingivitis mouthrinse.

nodes.label: Methyl Salicylate
nodes.summary: Component of the fixed-ratio essential oil antigingivitis mouthrinse.

nodes.label: Eucalyptol
nodes.summary: Component of the fixed-ratio essential oil antigingivitis mouthrinse.

nodes.label: Triclosan
nodes.summary: Antimicrobial clinically demonstrated to reduce gingivitis and useful for oral malodor.

nodes.label: Cetylpyridinium Chloride
nodes.summary: Antimicrobial clinically demonstrated to reduce gingivitis.

nodes.label: Pyrophosphate
nodes.summary: Most common anticalculus agent in tartar control toothpastes; interferes with calcium phosphate crystal growth.

nodes.label: Zinc Citrate
nodes.summary: Zinc salt used as anticalculus agent in tartar control toothpastes.

nodes.label: Zinc Chloride
nodes.summary: Antitartar agent in the one tartar control mouthrinse on the market.

nodes.label: Dental Erosion
nodes.summary: Dissolution of enamel and dentin by acids of intrinsic or external (non-bacterial) origin; depends on acid pH, titratable acidity and behaviors.

nodes.label: Gingivitis
nodes.summary: Reversible inflammation of the gums with bleeding, associated with plaque accumulation and Gram-negative anaerobes like Fusobacterium nucleatum and Prevotella intermedia.

nodes.label: Periodontitis
nodes.summary: Serious periodontal disease with severe inflammation, deeper pockets and irreversible alveolar bone loss; associated with Porphyromonas gingivalis; not an OTC indication.

nodes.label: Porphyromonas Gingivalis
nodes.summary: Particularly pathogenic bacterium in periodontitis-associated plaque.

nodes.label: Gram-Negative Anaerobic Bacteria
nodes.summary: Mature plaque bacteria (e.g. Fusobacterium nucleatum, Prevotella intermedia) producing volatile sulfur compounds, organic acids and endotoxins that drive gingivitis and malodor.

nodes.label: Volatile Sulfur Compounds
nodes.summary: Malodorous compounds such as H2S and methyl mercaptan produced by anaerobic oral bacteria; bound by copper, zinc and tin ions.

nodes.label: Dentin Hypersensitivity
nodes.summary: Pain from exposed dentin triggered by heat, cold, pressure or sugar; affects about one in seven people.

nodes.label: Hydrodynamic Theory
nodes.summary: Most accepted model of dentinal hypersensitivity: stimuli change fluid pressure in open tubules transmitted to pulp nerves as pain.

nodes.label: Gingival Recession
nodes.summary: Gum recession from periodontal disease or improper brushing that exposes root cementum and dentin.

nodes.label: Strontium Chloride
nodes.summary: Desensitizing agent that promotes blockage of open dentinal tubules.

nodes.label: Arginine
nodes.summary: Used with calcium carbonate in dentifrices to block open dentinal tubules.

nodes.label: Potassium Nitrate
nodes.summary: Desensitizer that reduces pulpal nerve sensitivity by depolarizing nerve membranes.

nodes.label: Dental Staining
nodes.summary: Intrinsic (within tooth) or extrinsic (chromogens from tea, coffee, tobacco, metal ions) tooth discoloration of cosmetic concern.

nodes.label: Tooth Whitening
nodes.summary: Removal of stain by abrasives or bleaching with peroxides or chlorine compounds; peroxide oral products not permitted in Canada.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Peroxide
nodes.summary: Peroxide bleaching agent used to reduce extrinsic or intrinsic dental stain.

nodes.label: Carbamide Peroxide
nodes.summary: Peroxide bleaching agent in tooth whitening products.

nodes.label: Chlorine Dioxide
nodes.summary: Chlorine compound used as tooth bleaching agent.

nodes.label: Abrasives
nodes.summary: Dentifrice systems that mechanically remove extrinsic stain; abrasivity must stay within a safe range.

nodes.label: Oral Malodor
nodes.summary: Bad breath; intrinsic mainly from anaerobic bacterial volatile sulfur compounds on tongue and plaque, extrinsic from ingested garlic, cheese, tobacco.

nodes.label: Sodium Bicarbonate
nodes.summary: Claimed to neutralize volatile malodorous compounds in oral products.

nodes.label: Xerostomia
nodes.summary: Dry mouth from reduced saliva flow due to systemic disease (Sjogren's), radiation, or over 200 drugs; leads to rampant caries and candidiasis.

nodes.label: Artificial Saliva
nodes.summary: Products with humectants, lubricants, buffers and sometimes fluoride to relieve sensation of oral dryness.

nodes.label: Aphthous Ulcer
nodes.summary: Canker sores: painful 2-10 mm crater-like lesions on tongue and buccal mucosa lasting 5-10 days; autoimmune origin most supported.

nodes.label: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
nodes.summary: Toothpaste surfactant suggested as a predisposing factor for canker sores.

nodes.label: Benzocaine
nodes.summary: Topical anesthetic used to reduce canker sore discomfort.

nodes.label: Lidocaine
nodes.summary: Topical anesthetic used to reduce canker sore discomfort.

nodes.label: Toothpaste
nodes.summary: Dentifrice delivering fluoride, anticalculus, antimicrobial, desensitizing and abrasive agents; fluoride toothpastes introduced in the US in the 1950s.

nodes.label: Mouthwash
nodes.summary: Mouthrinse delivering fluoride, antimicrobials or flavors for caries, gingivitis and malodor control.

nodes.label: Occlusal Sealant
nodes.summary: Sealants on pits and fissures that reduce caries by eliminating niches for S. mutans.

nodes.label: Mechanical Oral Hygiene
nodes.summary: Brushing and flossing that reduce plaque, calculus formation, gingivitis and malodor.

nodes.label: DMFT/DMFS Index
nodes.summary: Clinical caries index summing Decayed, Missing and Filled teeth or surfaces used in anticaries trials.

nodes.label: ICDAS
nodes.summary: International Caries Detection and Assessment System for classifying early caries lesions.

nodes.label: Quantitative Light-Induced Fluorescence
nodes.summary: Detection method for monitoring early caries lesions.

nodes.label: OTC Drug
nodes.summary: Over-the-counter drug category; anticaries fluoride products are regulated as drugs under US monograph 21 CFR Parts 310, 355 and 369.

nodes.label: FDA
nodes.summary: US Food and Drug Administration; concluded panel hearings on antiplaque/antigingivitis agents in 1998 and published recommendations in 2003.

nodes.label: Colgate-Palmolive
nodes.summary: Oral care company employing chapter author Roger Ellwood.

nodes.label: Feminine Rejuvenation
nodes.summary: Covers vulvar anatomy and innervation, sensory perception, and vulvar atrophy causes and physiology. Reviews OTC, estrogen and ospemifene treatments, and topical growth factors and adipose-derived stem cell secreted factors as a new cosmetic frontier.

nodes.label: Vulva
nodes.summary: Externally visible female genital region composed of mons veneris, labia majora, labia minora and clitoris; richly vascular like the face.

nodes.label: Labia Majora
nodes.summary: Two longitudinal skin folds rich in adipose tissue, sebaceous and sweat glands enclosing the vulvar cleft.

nodes.label: Labia Minora
nodes.summary: Thin pigmented skin folds without hair follicles, poor in sweat glands but rich in sebaceous glands.

nodes.label: Clitoris
nodes.summary: Small erectile organ of crura, body and glans; glans covered by over 8,000 nerve endings and protected by the clitoral hood.

nodes.label: Mons Veneris
nodes.summary: Fatty hair-covered prominence overlying the symphysis pubis.

nodes.label: Pudendal Nerve
nodes.summary: Nerve (S2-S4) whose perineal branch covers labia majora and whose deep branch supplies over 8,000 nerve endings of the glans clitoris.

nodes.label: Meissner Corpuscle
nodes.summary: Mechanoreceptor detecting transient light touch on vulva and extragenital sites.

nodes.label: Pacinian Corpuscle
nodes.summary: Mechanoreceptor detecting transient deeper pressure.

nodes.label: Merkel Cell
nodes.summary: Slowly adapting receptor responding to sustained touch such as texture or shape; possible target of estrogen effect on sensitivity.

nodes.label: Ruffini Receptor
nodes.summary: Slowly adapting mechanoreceptor responding to sustained touch.

nodes.label: Sensory Perception
nodes.summary: Touch, vibration and thermal perception most significantly affected by advancing age; vulvar touch thresholds 4.6-fold lower in normoestrogenic vs hypoestrogenic women.

nodes.label: Vulvar Atrophy
nodes.summary: Silent epidemic affecting up to 50% of postmenopausal women: thinning, loss of elasticity, decreased vascularity and nerve endings, dryness and inflammation, mainly from hypoestrogenism.

nodes.label: Menopause
nodes.summary: Natural cause of hypoestrogenic vulvar atrophy; vulvar mechanical sensitivity declines after menopause.

nodes.label: Estrogen
nodes.summary: Hormone with profound effect on vulvar touch sensitivity; topical low-dose estrogen is first-line pharmacologic treatment for vulvar atrophy, accelerating healing and decreasing inflammation.

nodes.label: Hypoestrogenism
nodes.summary: Low estrogen state from menopause, ovarian failure, aromatase inhibitors, GnRH agonists or breastfeeding causing vulvar atrophy and loss of sensitivity.

nodes.label: Lichen Sclerosus
nodes.summary: Develops with chronic vulvar inflammation, involving skin and mucous membranes of vulvar and rectal area.

nodes.label: Kraurosis Vulvae
nodes.summary: Progressive sclerosing atrophy with stenosis of the vaginal orifice and effacement of labia minora and clitoris.

nodes.label: Dyspareunia
nodes.summary: Painful intercourse; not due to lack of arousal; ospemifene approved for it.

nodes.label: Chronic Inflammation in Aging Skin
nodes.summary: Older skin has higher interleukin-1, interleukin-6 and TNF-alpha, creating a vicious cycle of inflammation, repair and itching in vulvar skin.

nodes.label: Interleukin-1
nodes.summary: Pro-inflammatory cytokine elevated in older skin.

nodes.label: Interleukin-6
nodes.summary: Pro-inflammatory cytokine elevated in older skin.

nodes.label: TNF-Alpha
nodes.summary: Pro-inflammatory cytokine elevated in older skin.

nodes.label: Skin Aging
nodes.summary: Age changes include lower elasticity and tensile strength, reduced dermal and epidermal thickness, vascularity, hydration and sensory perception, flattened DEJ, increased permeability and slower wound healing.

nodes.label: Aromatase Inhibitor
nodes.summary: Endocrine therapy used by breast cancer patients that causes ovarian dysfunction and vulvar atrophy.

nodes.label: Vaginal Moisturizers and Lubricants
nodes.summary: OTC products lacking definitive efficacy data, none designed for the vulva; may contain irritants like propylene glycol, parabens, perfumes, benzocaine.

nodes.label: Propylene Glycol
nodes.summary: Ingredient in OTC lubricants that can cause sensitivity in inflamed mucous membranes.

nodes.label: Parabens
nodes.summary: Preservatives in some OTC vaginal products considered potentially irritating.

nodes.label: Mineral Oil
nodes.summary: Petroleum-based product that can interfere with condom use and is best avoided.

nodes.label: Petrolatum
nodes.summary: Petroleum jelly; can interfere with condom use.

nodes.label: Ospemifene
nodes.summary: FDA-approved oral non-estrogen SERM for dyspareunia; side effects include hot flashes; risk of endometrial cancer, stroke and blood clots.

nodes.label: Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator
nodes.summary: Compounds acting as estrogen agonists or antagonists depending on tissue type.

nodes.label: Hormone Replacement Therapy
nodes.summary: Systemic HRT whose use dropped after the Women's Health Initiative showed small increased breast cancer, heart attack and stroke risks.

nodes.label: North American Menopause Society
nodes.summary: Issued evidence-based position statement recommending local estrogen treatment for vaginal atrophy.

nodes.label: Growth Factors
nodes.summary: Topical growth factors and peptides help reverse skin aging though mainly used in wound healing; include TGF-beta1, PDGF, KGF, bFGF, HGF, VEGF.

nodes.label: Peptides
nodes.summary: Topical peptides play a role in reversing skin aging; mass-produced from adult stem cell growth media.

nodes.label: Adipose-Derived Stem Cell
nodes.summary: Adult stem cells from subcutaneous fat secreting cytokines and growth factors (paracrine effect); injection increased collagen expression 40x in pig skin and reduced UVB wrinkles.

nodes.label: Stem Cells
nodes.summary: Immature precursor cells capable of self-renewal and multi-lineage differentiation; adult stem cells have fewer ethical and control issues than embryonic.

nodes.label: Paracrine Effect
nodes.summary: Stem cells secrete growth factors that activate neighboring cells to exhibit diverse pharmacologic actions.

nodes.label: Human Adipocyte Conditioned Media Extract
nodes.summary: INCI name for ADSC-derived peptide extract approved by CTFA in September 2006; topical AAPE gave good-to-excellent wrinkle improvement in 47% of subjects.

nodes.label: TGF-Beta 1
nodes.summary: Transforming growth factor in stem cell conditioned media; linked to whitening effect of ADSCs.

nodes.label: VEGF
nodes.summary: Vascular endothelial growth factor promoting new blood vessel formation; in ADSC conditioned media.

nodes.label: Superoxide Dismutase
nodes.summary: Antioxidant enzyme in ADSC conditioned media protecting skin from oxidative damage.

nodes.label: Kinetin
nodes.summary: Isolated from herring sperm DNA in 1955 with natural antioxidant properties.

nodes.label: Collagen
nodes.summary: Dermal protein; stem cells and their factors increase collagen content and synthesis.

nodes.label: Wrinkles
nodes.summary: Sign of skin aging; ADSC injection and topical secreted factors showed anti-wrinkle effects.

nodes.label: Wound Healing
nodes.summary: Slower with age; main use of growth factors; ADSC secretory factors promote it.

nodes.label: Personal Care Products Council
nodes.summary: Formerly CTFA; approved INCI name Human Adipocyte Conditioned Media Extract in 2006.

nodes.label: Sustainability and Eco-Responsibility: A Global Approach
nodes.summary: Covers Part 12 of the sustainability focus book: defining sustainability and open innovation for sustainability, a botanist's view of sustainable wild harvesting and benefit sharing, the Herboretum network, local cultivation for carbon footprint reduction, plant cell cultures producing phenylpropanoids, eco-responsible plant extraction and formulation, and green industrial solutions like zeodration and wetland gardens.

nodes.label: Triple Bottom Line
nodes.summary: Measuring company success equally on people, planet and profit, coined by John Elkington in 1998.

nodes.label: Eco-Responsibility
nodes.summary: Long-term production management balancing raw materials, process energy, waste, effluents and product impacts; described as the 'eco-responsibility tsunami' following the green wave and organic tide.

nodes.label: Eco-Design
nodes.summary: Eco-conception of ingredients and products that generates innovative concepts and new technologies.

nodes.label: Open Innovation
nodes.summary: Methodology leveraging internal and external technology assets to accelerate innovation, relying on transparency and collaboration.

nodes.label: Open Innovation for Sustainability
nodes.summary: Application of open innovation to sustainability goals; OIS companies collaborate with competitors and NGOs, embrace transparency and share green IP, adopting a more complete OI model.

nodes.label: Transparency
nodes.summary: Full disclosure of ingredients, packaging and partners and external auditing; required by both sustainability and open innovation.

nodes.label: Collaboration
nodes.summary: Partnering across supply chains, competitors and NGOs; inherent to OI and required by the complexity of sustainability.

nodes.label: Greenwashing
nodes.summary: Overinflating a product's or company's green attributes; fear of accusation can prevent sustainable innovation; OI helps overcome the perception.

nodes.label: Six Traits of Sustainable Companies
nodes.summary: OIS companies are systemic, enterprise-level, committed, collaborative, invested and transparent.

nodes.label: Social Auditing
nodes.summary: Quantifying and publicly disclosing green efforts under pressure from employees and consumers.

nodes.label: Green IP Sharing
nodes.summary: Donating or licensing sustainability IP for modest fees, e.g. WBCSD Eco-Patent Commons and Nike's GreenXChange.

nodes.label: Nike
nodes.summary: Developed a $6 million Environmental Apparel Design Tool assessing footprint of technologies and shared it with industry.

nodes.label: Superordinate Goal
nodes.summary: Resource scarcity creates a goal that normally opposed parties (competitors, NGOs) agree to work on together.

nodes.label: Resource Scarcity
nodes.summary: Limited natural resources from population growth (toward 9 billion) and destruction of rare plants; a driver pushing companies to embrace sustainability.

nodes.label: EU Cosmetics Regulation
nodes.summary: European Union regulations requiring documentation of toxicological properties, driving data sharing from larger to smaller companies; European Cosmetic Directives.

nodes.label: Ethnobotany
nodes.summary: Study of plant use by traditional peoples; the ethnobotanically directed survey evaluates traditional uses in assays to develop actives.

nodes.label: Plant Collection Surveys
nodes.summary: Random (shotgun), phylogenetic and ethnobotanically directed survey strategies for discovering plant actives.

nodes.label: Good Botanical Practices
nodes.summary: Proper collection, identification and permanent documentation of plant-based ingredients.

nodes.label: Convention on Biological Diversity
nodes.summary: UN-sponsored convention calling for compensation of communities and source countries for traditional knowledge and materials used commercially.

nodes.label: Nagoya Protocol
nodes.summary: Access and benefit-sharing protocol under which wild collection could expose companies to biopiracy lawsuits.

nodes.label: Access and Benefit Sharing
nodes.summary: Compensating people and communities for knowledge leading to commercial plant use, including remuneration and involvement in cultivation.

nodes.label: Biopiracy
nodes.summary: Unauthorized use of genetic resources or traditional knowledge; wild collection may face biopiracy lawsuits under Nagoya.

nodes.label: Traditional Knowledge
nodes.summary: Indigenous knowledge of plant uses (anti-inflammatory, cleansing, sunscreens, wound healing) guiding discovery; must be truthfully represented in marketing.

nodes.label: Sustainable Harvest
nodes.summary: Harvesting non-timber products indefinitely with negligible impact on plant populations (Peters); steps: species selection, forest inventory, yield studies, harvest levels, monitoring.

nodes.label: Non-Timber Forest Product
nodes.summary: Fruits, nuts, latexes and other forest products; sustainable harvest levels poorly known for most.

nodes.label: Wild Harvesting
nodes.summary: Collecting plants from the wild; can cause overharvesting and extinction (e.g. rosewood); not considered sustainable compared with cultivation.

nodes.label: Overharvesting
nodes.summary: Harvesting beyond regeneration capacity, threatening species such as Brazil nut and rosewood with extinction.

nodes.label: Brazil Nut
nodes.summary: Bertholletia excelsa; ~200,000 people harvest ~20,000 tons yearly from Amazon; overharvest prevents tree regeneration.

nodes.label: Brosimum Alicastrum
nodes.summary: Central/South American tree needing over 1.5 million seeds for one tree to reach reproduction; fruit overharvest could cause extinction.

nodes.label: Marula
nodes.summary: Sclerocarya birrea, South African tree supplying food, timber, medicine and oil for personal care; governance combines statutory law and traditional custom.

nodes.label: Biodiversity
nodes.summary: Reservoir of plant molecules for cosmetics; over 300,000 flowering plant species with ~70,000 undiscovered; protecting it is life insurance for humanity and industry.

nodes.label: Herboretum Association
nodes.summary: Formed 2004; nine-hectare open-air plant laboratory at St. Ay near Orleans with over 1,000 plant species, thematic and ecological gardens and fauna observatories.

nodes.label: Palm Oil
nodes.summary: Its use including in biofuels has destroyed large parts of Indonesian and Malaysian rainforest and biodiversity.

nodes.label: Corporate Social Responsibility
nodes.summary: Annual evaluation of large companies' contribution to sustainable development, favoring eco-responsible partners.

nodes.label: Phytocosmetics
nodes.summary: Plant-based cosmetics industry using medicinal and aromatic plants such as cornflower, milk thistle, burdock, soapwort.

nodes.label: Cornflower
nodes.summary: Plant used for soothing, softening eye care; grown in the Beauce region.

nodes.label: Evening Primrose
nodes.summary: Cosmetic plant of the Beauce region used to moisturize dry skin.

nodes.label: Local Cultivation
nodes.summary: Growing plant biomass close to processing facilities to reduce transport and carbon footprint; cultivated plants preferred over wild for identity, safety and sustainability.

nodes.label: Plant Identification
nodes.summary: Scientific binomial name, plant part, botanical (macro/microscopic), phytochemical (TLC, HPLC, GC) and genomic identification of plant raw materials.

nodes.label: Genomic Identification
nodes.summary: PCR-amplified short DNA fragments (especially mitochondrial) to authenticate species, variety and origin, ensuring traceability and detecting adulteration.

nodes.label: Chromatography
nodes.summary: TLC, HPLC and GC used for phytochemical identification and standardization of extracts.

nodes.label: CITES
nodes.summary: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, adopted 1973 in Washington and signed by 175 countries; classifies endangered plants in three appendices.

nodes.label: Rosewood
nodes.summary: Aniba rosaeodora; overexploited in French Guiana for essential oil by distillers clear-cutting trees until protected status and replanting.

nodes.label: Good Agricultural Practices
nodes.summary: Quality assurance for medicinal plants covering seeds, cultivation, crop rotation, minimal agrochemicals, optimal picking time, and trained personnel.

nodes.label: Plant Breeding
nodes.summary: Mass selection and cross-breeding (aided by molecular markers) to create varieties with high yield, disease resistance and high active content.

nodes.label: German Chamomile
nodes.summary: Matricaria recutita L.; selected variety has 3% vs 1% flavonoids, needing three times less plant mass and giving 65% lower carbon footprint.

nodes.label: Flavonoids
nodes.summary: Active ingredients of German chamomile flower; synthesized in chloroplasts.

nodes.label: Organic Farming
nodes.summary: Based on health, ecology, fairness and care; avoids synthetic chemicals and GMOs; supply security, yield and cost limit its use in cosmetics.

nodes.label: Sustainable Farming
nodes.summary: Conventional farming controlling inputs of fertilizers and pesticides; most cosmetic plants come from it; requires checks for pesticides, heavy metals, mycotoxins, PAHs.

nodes.label: Pesticides
nodes.summary: Contaminants of plant raw materials that must stay below authorized limits; absent in plant cell culture.

nodes.label: Heavy Metals
nodes.summary: Toxic contaminants some plants fix selectively from soil; soils must be analyzed.

nodes.label: Mycotoxins
nodes.summary: Highly toxic fungal metabolites such as aflatoxins and ochratoxins (LD50 often below ug/kg) formed in poorly stored humid plants.

nodes.label: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
nodes.summary: Highly toxic contaminants produced by burning fossil fuels; drying equipment must not generate them.

nodes.label: Plant Drying
nodes.summary: Most common plant preservation method reducing water to ~12% to stop enzymatic and microbial deterioration; erysimum optimal at 75 C.

nodes.label: Sinigrin
nodes.summary: Glucosinolate in erysimum stored in vacuoles; degraded by myrosinase upon tissue laceration unless dried at 75 C.

nodes.label: Myrosinase
nodes.summary: Plant enzyme degrading sinigrin into volatile toxic molecules as a natural defense; inactivated at 75 C drying.

nodes.label: Comfrey
nodes.summary: Symphytum officinale; root widely used in cosmetics while the flower contains toxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids.

nodes.label: Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids
nodes.summary: Toxic alkaloids found in comfrey flowers.

nodes.label: Plant Stem Cell
nodes.summary: Meristem cells maintaining totipotency; cultured callus and suspension cells resemble undifferentiated meristem cells.

nodes.label: Totipotency
nodes.summary: Embryonic ability of plant meristem cells to originate all differentiated plant structures; regained by wounded somatic cells.

nodes.label: Elicitation
nodes.summary: Abiotic (UV, temperature) or biotic (chitosan, methyl jasmonate, salicylic acid) elicitors up-regulate secondary metabolites like phenylpropanoids in plant cell cultures.

nodes.label: Secondary Metabolites
nodes.summary: Plant compounds for adaptation and protection (terpenoids, alkaloids, phenylpropanoids) often present at low levels.

nodes.label: Phenylpropanoids
nodes.summary: Phenylalanine-derived polyphenols that absorb UV, repel herbivores, and act as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, photoprotecting and antimicrobial cosmetic agents.

nodes.label: Echinacoside
nodes.summary: Phenylpropanoid from Echinacea angustifolia (1-2% of dry root) produced by plant cell culture; used in anti-aging products.

nodes.label: Echinacea Angustifolia
nodes.summary: Plant requiring 3-4 years cultivation for roots; cell cultures produce echinacoside.

nodes.label: Verbascoside
nodes.summary: Phenylpropanoid glycoside (acteoside) containing caffeic acid and hydroxytyrosol; inhibits NF-kB, COX-2, iNOS and activates Nrf2; produced by Syringa vulgaris, Buddleja davidii cell cultures; used for lightening.

nodes.label: Chlorogenic Acid
nodes.summary: Ester of caffeic and quinic acids; inhibits NF-kB and AP-1, activates Nrf2, decreases chemical carcinogenesis in animal models.

nodes.label: Caffeic Acid
nodes.summary: Phenylpropanoid that is an excellent oxidative radical scavenger.

nodes.label: Taxol
nodes.summary: Terpenoid anticancer drug that cannot be chemically synthesized economically; produced via plant cell culture.

nodes.label: Edelweiss
nodes.summary: Leontopodium alpinum; plant from which cell cultures were developed for phenylpropanoid extracts.

nodes.label: Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Compounds scavenging reactive species and chelating metals; phenylpropanoids and rosemary extract act as antioxidants.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species
nodes.summary: Free radicals directly scavenged by phenylpropanoids and their glycosides.

nodes.label: NF-kB
nodes.summary: Inflammatory transcription factor pathway inhibited by verbascoside and chlorogenic acid.

nodes.label: Nrf2
nodes.summary: Transcription factor driving ARE-mediated phase 2 detoxifying enzymes; activated by verbascoside and chlorogenic acid.

nodes.label: COX-2
nodes.summary: Cyclooxygenase-2 inflammatory enzyme inhibited by verbascoside.

nodes.label: FAO
nodes.summary: UN Food and Agriculture Organization; endorsed plant cell culture technology for secondary metabolite production.

nodes.label: IRB SpA
nodes.summary: Italian company that fine-tuned plant cell culture technology for cosmetic phenylpropanoids.

nodes.label: Plant Extraction
nodes.summary: Maceration, separation (filtration) and concentration of actives using solvents; eco-responsible extraction uses biodegradable water and ethanol and recycles solvents.

nodes.label: Ethanol
nodes.summary: Biodegradable extraction solvent produced from renewable sugar cane, beet, wheat or corn; recycled by distillation.

nodes.label: Butylene Glycol
nodes.summary: Petrochemical solvent-carrier for extracts that hinders easy plant waste disposal.

nodes.label: Propanediol
nodes.summary: Propylene glycol alternative obtained by biofermentation of corn.

nodes.label: Glycerin
nodes.summary: Carrier (not an effective maceration solvent) from local rapeseed; avoids preservatives by preventing germ growth.

nodes.label: Spray Drying
nodes.summary: Fast high-temperature drying needing carriers like maltodextrin or lactose that dilute actives.

nodes.label: Lyophilization
nodes.summary: Deep-freeze vacuum drying with high energy consumption and refrigerating gases.

nodes.label: Zeodration
nodes.summary: Vacuum drying at <=40 C where water vapor is adsorbed onto 4-angstrom zeolites, whose exothermic reaction heats the product; low energy, no refrigerants, yields native carrier-free extracts.

nodes.label: Zeolites
nodes.summary: Crystallized clays adsorbing up to 30% of their mass in water; regenerated at 250 C; used in zeodration.

nodes.label: Maltodextrin
nodes.summary: Carrier used in spray drying that dilutes actives and adds sugars.

nodes.label: Organic Certification
nodes.summary: Certification designed for agricultural products, complex to extend to cosmetics; easily applied to essential oils and cold-pressed oils, harder for floral waters and extracts.

nodes.label: Ecocert
nodes.summary: Organic certification body; transesterification is an Ecocert-acceptable process.

nodes.label: Genetically Modified Organism
nodes.summary: Traceability concern mainly for vegetable oils from industrial crops (wheat, sunflower, palm); medicinal plants mostly unmodified.

nodes.label: Traceability
nodes.summary: Tracking from seed through field, harvest, drying and powdering to product; supported by genomic identification.

nodes.label: Vegetable Oils
nodes.summary: Replacing mineral oils in cosmetics; improved to lower peroxide index, color and odor; cold-pressed oils oxidize less.

nodes.label: Jojoba Wax
nodes.summary: Replacement for whale fat, grown in Arizona desert and now cultivated in Negev and Argentina.

nodes.label: Shea Butter
nodes.summary: African vegetable butter for richer touch; long transport impacts carbon footprint.

nodes.label: Flaxseed Oil
nodes.summary: Granolin project oil rich in linoleic and linolenic acids from reintroduced flax cultivation in central France.

nodes.label: Milk Thistle
nodes.summary: Plant grown near Chartres: seeds give silymarin, and seed cake yields omega-6-rich oil transesterified into a silicone-substitute mono-ester.

nodes.label: Silymarin
nodes.summary: Liver-protecting medicine extracted from milk thistle seeds.

nodes.label: Silicones
nodes.summary: Touch modifiers of consumer concern; plant mono-esters proposed as substitutes.

nodes.label: Rosemary Extract
nodes.summary: Plant antioxidant performing well in oily phases of formulations.

nodes.label: Salicylic Acid
nodes.summary: Natural-source preservative on all positive lists showing excellent results in aqueous systems and emulsions.

nodes.label: Preservatives
nodes.summary: Needed to keep extracts germ-free but negatively perceived by consumers; glycerin carriers and flash pasteurization reduce need.

nodes.label: Floral Water
nodes.summary: Distillation by-product of essential oils; easy organic extract but hard to preserve; can replace deionized water.

nodes.label: Phthalates
nodes.summary: Ingredients of consumer concern; incompatible with green claims.

nodes.label: REACH
nodes.summary: EU chemicals regulation measuring substance environmental impact; cosmetic ingredients comply while food-grade products don't.

nodes.label: Granolin Project
nodes.summary: Cosmetic Valley initiative reintroducing flaxseed cultivation in central France for full biomass use (oil and fiber insulation).

nodes.label: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy
nodes.summary: BSE crisis led cosmetics to abandon animal-derived ingredients, reviving interest in plants.

nodes.label: Wetland Restoration
nodes.summary: Alban Muller Group's 4,500 m2 water and biodiversity gardens returning 100,000 L/day of treated effluent to ponds, attracting amphibians, birds and bees.

nodes.label: Good Manufacturing Practices
nodes.summary: GMP standards for all products; suspension cell cultures are more GMP-compliant.

nodes.label: HACCP
nodes.summary: Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point norms for food products.

nodes.label: Biofermentation
nodes.summary: Emerging technology to benefit from natural molecules, e.g. producing propanediol from corn.
